reason: The brand's typeface (Phase 1). SIL Open Font License 1.1: fonts may be bundled with any software, AGPL included; the font stays under the OFL. Its package.json names the license in prose, not SPDX.

Through ut_pex (the torrent engine's peer exchange, ADR 0037). Its package.json says "BSD" without a variant and its README's Licence section says MIT (github.com/bencevans/node-compact2string); either is permissive and compatible with AGPL-3.0.

Through juice, which mjml-core uses to inline the emails' CSS (checkpoint 8b, docs/product/emails.md). Its package.json says "MIT (http://mootools.net/license.txt)": MIT, written with the MooTools license's address rather than as an SPDX id. MIT is compatible with AGPL-3.0.

Through reqwest's rustls, the desktop app's HTTPS to servers (4.4a). Mozilla's root certificates as data, under CDLA-Permissive-2.0, which lets the data be used and shared with its notice and puts no condition on the program that uses it (cdla.dev/permissive-2-0, section 3), so it's compatible with AGPL-3.0.
